title: VQE with a Hardware-Efficient Ansatz
summary: Find the H₂ ground state with a general multi-parameter ansatz instead of a chemistry-inspired one.
objectives: Build a layered ansatz from rotations and a ladder of CNOT gates, with no chemistry in it
Compare it with the chemistry ansatz by number of angles and by what it knows about the molecule
Say why starting every angle at zero stalls the training
mission: Show that a circuit with no chemistry in it can still reach the H₂ ground state. Reach an energy within chemical accuracy (1.6 mHa) of the exact value using at most 16 rotation angles and no excitation gates. The intended layout is the Hartree–Fock state, 3 layers of R_Y on every qubit each followed by CNOT gates on neighbours (0-1, 1-2, 2-3), and a final R_Y layer; train theta with qml.AdamOptimizer and record the energy after each step.

prediction.question: In the ansatz with 3 layers, every angle is set to 0, so only the CNOT ladders act on the Hartree–Fock state |1100⟩. Which basis state does the circuit prepare?
options: |1100⟩ itself: the rotations are zero, so nothing changes
|1010⟩, after the three ladders have moved the bits
|0011⟩, the other state of the chemistry ansatz
prediction.explanation: A CNOT ladder is a fixed permutation of bit strings, and with zero rotations it is the only thing that acts. Ladder 1 takes 1100 to 1000, ladder 2 takes 1000 to 1111, and ladder 3 takes 1111 to 1010. That state has energy −0.531 Ha and is an eigenstate of H, so the gradient is zero there and the optimizer cannot leave it.

hints: What does the circuit need to do before the first rotation? It has to prepare the Hartree–Fock state, so that the electron count starts right.

Keep a counter k of the angle you are using. In each of the LAYERS rounds apply qml.RY(theta[k], wires=q) on every qubit, increasing k each time, then qml.CNOT(wires=[q, q + 1]) for q in range(3). Add one more rotation layer at the end.
The counter ends at 16, the length of theta. Train with qml.AdamOptimizer(0.1), about 150 steps, and append float(circuit(theta)) to energies at each step.

messages.wrong_qubits: H₂ in this basis has 4 spin orbitals, so the circuit needs 4 qubits, and yours has {count}.

challenge.mission: The theory of this lesson says that the all-zero start cannot be trained. Show it with numbers. With all 16 angles at zero, compute energy_zero (the energy of the circuit) and grad_norm_zero (the norm of its 16-component gradient), then run Adam for at least 10 steps from zero and keep the energy after each step in energies_zero. After that, train from small random angles as in the mission and reach chemical accuracy: theta and energies as before. The validator recomputes the energy and the gradient at zero from your circuit and compares them with your numbers.
hints: Evaluate the circuit with np.zeros(16), and take the gradient of the circuit at that point with qml.grad. What energy do you get, and what does it tell you about the state?
With zero rotations only the CNOT ladders act on the Hartree–Fock state. A gradient that is exactly zero gives Adam nothing to scale, so every step is zero too.
Use a fresh optimizer for each run, and keep energies for the second run only: the check reads its last value against the final theta. A short zero run (20 steps) keeps the total time low.
